text:
Judd Caulfield took the long road. A fifth-round pick of the Penguins in 2019, he went through North Dakota and the AHL's San Diego Gulls before getting his first NHL game this fall at 25. Twenty-two games in, he has four goals, 11 points and 80 hits, and Anaheim keeps giving him more: his ice time is up 3:13 a night over his last ten.

Those ten games have been a grind on the scoresheet, no goals and three points where our numbers expected about 5.4. But this is the kind of cold spell we like to see. He has 2.8 expected goals on his own shots in that stretch, right where his usual rate says it should be, so the looks are there and the pucks just haven't gone in. His 1.14 individual expected goals per 60 is a genuine net-front number.

The worry is the bigger picture: Anaheim gets only 45% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice. Watch whether the extra minutes come with better linemates or just more work.
headline: Judd Caulfield, 25-year-old rookie, keeps knocking
